title: Edit 3D Garment
content: **List of Contents** Edit Style Line Scale/ Move Style Line Draw Style Line **Objective** Edit 3D garment easily by moving point and line by keeping its shape. **** **Location** 3D Toolbar **▶![Scale StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431208484249) Edit StyleLine **Tool 3D Toolbar **▶![Scale StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431208484249) Scale StyleLine **Tool 3D Toolbar **▶![Add StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431224771481) Add StyleLine **Tool ## **Operation** **Edit Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear with a black outline. 3. Click on the point ▶ drag and move. → The line and the point sewn are moved together. 4. Or click on the segment ▶ drag it. → The curvature of the line is now adjustable. **Scale/ Move Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear translucent. 3. Click on the segment ▶ drag it. → The garment is scaled or moved with the sewn lines in the drag direction. **Draw Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear translucent. 3. Hover on a Segment, a blue point will appear, click to start the new Style Line. → A point is added to the selected point. 4. Draw a curved line by clicking within the pattern piece, then double click on the segment where you want the new Style Line to end, or draw a straight line by double-clicking the endpoint. → The pattern piece cut along the style line added. **※ Note:** \- The function that allows you to scale or move one side of the sewn lines is excluded in the 6.2 version. The new feature with the improvement of usability will be provided. \- While Editing/Scaling/Moving Style Line, right click to enter the desired dimension. (ver 7.1)
content_description: "Effortlessly edit and customize 3D garments by manipulating style lines and points for precise adjustments and enhancements."

title: I deleted my account. How can I reactivate my account?
content: **Question** I deleted my account. How can I reactivate my account? **Answer** No, deleted accounts cannot be recovered. When an account is deleted, your CLO account information is permanently removed, along with your previous subscription and payment history. Therefore, please consider carefully before considering deleting your account.
content_description: This webpage informs users about the irreversibility of deleted accounts and emphasizes the importance of careful consideration before account deletion.

title: How can I check my payment history?
content: **Question** How can I check my payment history? **Answer** To check your payment history, please follow the indicated guideline below. 1. Click your user ID on the upper right of the main page after sign-in. 2. Go to the "[Billing page](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/billing)" and click the "Billing details".
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to check your payment history.

title: How can I change my payment method?
content: **Question** How can I change the payment method? How can I remove my payment method? **Answer** To change the payment method, your subscription should be active. 1. Go to your **[Billing page](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/billing)** 2. Click the "Update billing information" button and the "Update" button. 3. Change your card information and click the "Save" button. Regarding the deletion of payment information, your payment details will be automatically removed as long as your subscription is canceled. As long as your subscription is deactivated, your payment information is not stored. *The changed payment information will be reflected on your next subscription. *In case your license is not currently active, you can only update your payment method when you [purchase a new license.](https://www.clo3d.com/en/plans) *Alipay users cannot change the payment method and need to cancel and resubscribe with a new payment method. *If you have an issue regarding changing the payment method, please reach out to CLO via **[Contact Us.](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus)**
content_description: This page provides step-by-step instructions for changing or removing your payment method for your subscription.

title: Brush Pinching
content: **New in 2026.1** ## **** Apply brush stroke-based pinching to intuitively deform garment surfaces. **** 1. Click ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59627243581593) the Simulate tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Click and hold ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59627227583769)the Quick Pinching tool for more than 2 seconds, then select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59627243584409)the Brush Pinching tool from the expanded tool menu. 3. Hover over the garment in the 3D window. 4. Click and drag to apply pinching along the accumulated brush stroke path based on the Strength value. 5. Set the Brush and Pinching options if needed. **Brush** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Size** | Adjusts the brush size. **Focal Radius** | Adjusts the size of the focal area. **Lazy Distance** | Adjusts the length of the Stroke Trail. **Display Weights** | Displays the weighted area along the accumulated brush stroke. **Pinching** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Strength** | Adjusts the strength of the pinching deformation. **Push Inward** | Applies pinching inward. **Average Radius** | Adjusts the reference area used to stabilize deformation.
content_description: Discover how to intuitively deform garment surfaces using the new brush stroke-based pinching feature in CLO 3D, introduced in version 2026.1.

title: Set Sublayer (Pattern)
content: ### **Objective** In the 2D window, set an order between two selected Patterns to achieve stable simulation for a 3D Garment with multiple layers such as windbreaker, utilitarian jacket, and more. **Location ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![set_sublayer.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024684968) **Set Sublayer** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![set_sublayer.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024684968) **Set Sublayer ** → Only Pattern outlines appear in the 2D window. 2. Click a Pattern to be arranged on top. → The selected Pattern's outline turns red and a red arrow follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click another Pattern that should be arranged below the first Pattern clicked. → A black arrow is created connecting two selected Patterns. → A plus sign appears at the center of the arrow to indicate the order of two Patterns. 4. To change the order between two Patterns, use the same tool and select the plus sign. → The plus sign changes to a minus sign and the Pattern order is changed.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for setting the order of Patterns in the 2D window to ensure stable simulation of multi-layered 3D garments.

title: What does each mode represent?
content: Modes can be switched through a dropdown menu at the top right of the CLO interface. Previous versions included more modes which have meanhwhile moved into being accessible through the main menu. Three remain at their original location: **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000306927/_____.png) Simulation Mode:** Create and edit patterns in the 2D window, working on garments, changing avatar poses, etc. in the 3D window. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000306987/_______.png)** **Print Layout Mode:** Manually order patterns on prints to match texture placements in the 3D window and calculate fabric consumption. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000303148/_____.png) Emulator Mode:** Create physical properties for fabrics after measuring them out with the CLO Fabric Kit hardware.
content_description: This web page provides an overview of the CLO interface modes, detailing how to switch between them and their specific functions for garment design and fabric creation.

title: Use Layer (Drape Additional Garment)
content: ### **Objective** This function allows easier Simulation when setting which layer to get in/outward among overlapped multiple layers. By using this function, taking out inaccurately inwardly simulated patterns such as pockets and buttons, gets easier. In addition, adding additional outerwear on top of garments such as dress and shirts. The default layer value of zero ('0') means the layer function is being off. In that state, the arrangement order of the Patterns gets decided. **Operation** 1. Select a Pattern in the 3D window to set a layer with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005642368/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** tool. → Pattern property appears in the Property Editor. 2. In the Simulation ▶ **Layer** properties, enter the larer value than the inside pattern for the pattern to be placed on the outside, and enter the smaller value than the outside pattern for the pattern to be placed inside. → The pattern with layer is displayed in color. **※Note:** Right-click on the background of the 3D window and click **Show/Hide Colors****▶ Layer** to hide color. (ver 7.3[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142607041305)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=rDrQIfsgUDAq_FC5&t=1372)) 3. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005642388/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulation** tool. → The order is applied and simulated according to the set layer values. 4. Once simulating is complete in the desired order, change the layer values for all patterns to 0 for a stable simulation. → The simulated result will remain in order.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the layer function in 3D simulation to effectively manage overlapping garment patterns, ensuring accurate representation of design elements like pockets and buttons.

title: How can I join CLO Discord?
content: **Account Creation** * Go to [https://discord.com/](https://discord.com/) * Create an account * Choose how you want to access Discord * Option 1: Choose to download the Discord app for your desktop * Option 2: Choose to access Discord in your browser **Joining the CLO Discord Server** * Copy the CLO Discord server invitation link to your Clipboard * <https://bit.ly/CLOOFFICIAL> * Open the Discord Desktop App * Click on the Add a Server Button on the left side of the interface ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814772432921) * In the **Create a Server** Pop-up, Click **Join a Server** at the bottom ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814776251033) * Paste the server link in the**Invite Link** field, then click**Join Server ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814830874649) ** * The CLO icon will now appear on the left side of your interface. ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814848111897) * Go to the **Notice** channels on the left side. Please read the **Rules** and **Read me First** text channels ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814904331289) * Go to the **Self-Roles** channel and react with the blue dot to gain full access to all of the CLO channels ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814874720281) ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814908382617) * You will now see all of the different CLO text channels. Happy CLOing!
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating a Discord account and joining the CLO Discord server to connect with the community.

title: Register Avatar Accessory
content: #### Register an avatar accessory file or convert a pattern into an accessory. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44760225403161) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/TApSQk7tXUY?si=MWBU0VR5tacpweKs) 1. Open the avatar file to register an accessory. 2. Click Main Menu » Avatar » **Register Accessory**. 3. After setting the options below, click the Save button. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Rigging Type** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55471518449049) Select whether the accessory to register is defined for the CLO default Standard or if it utilizes a general Rigging method. * Standard: Registers accessories according to the types defined in the CLO default avatar. * Rigged: Registers rigged accessories without a specific type. When loading the file, joints with the same name as the avatar's will be automatically merged. **Accessory Type** | Select the type of the accessory.(Hair, Shoes, Earring, Glasses) **📝Note:** This can be selected only when the rigging type is set to "Standard." **Object** | Select the type of the object (file and pattern) to register. You can load and select objects in the 3D window and adjust their positions directly. **File** | Select the path to the hair and shoe files to register. **Scale/ Axis Conversion** | Change the size and axis of the loaded file and check it simulatenously. **Pattern** | Select the pattern you want to convert to the accessory. However, the pattern to be converted must be created in advance before the accessory registration is proceeded. **📝****Note:** After selecting the pattern to be converted to an accessory, you can also right-click the 3D pattern ▶ Convert ▶ to Avatar Accessory menu. **Option** | **Mirror Creation** | If you register shoes and earrings, it automatically creates the opposite object. Inverted relative to the central axis of the avatar. **Thumbnail** | **Auto** | Apply the thumbnail image automatically. **Custom** | Apply the desired image as the thumbnail. 4. Click**Save** button to save as the Avatar Accessory file. #### **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44760225407513)** Easily register shoes without limitations like left/right distinction or heel assignment. 1. Set Accessory Type to **Shoes** **» Heels** in Register Accessory window. 2. When opening a shoe file, CLO will automatically differentiate between the left and right shoes. 3. For heels, follow these steps to ensure a proper fit: 3-1. In the 3D window, click on the heel meshes of the shoe. If the heel has multiple meshes, select them all at once by clicking and dragging to define the area. 3-2. Right-click and click **Set as Heels**. If incorrectly set, right-click and click **Unset Heel.** **![Shoes.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44762280722841)** 4. Click**Save** button to save as the Avatar Accessory file.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for registering avatar accessory files and converting patterns into accessories within CLO 3D, complete with step-by-step instructions and helpful video resources.

title: Gluing
content: **New in 2026.0** **Glue Fill** **Glue Brush** **Sticker** **Edit Gluing** Bond two pattern pieces together by adding glue to the entire pattern or a designated area. This feature allows secondary pieces like pockets, labels, or reinforcements to follow the movement and deformation of a base pattern during simulation. The Glue tools provide multiple methods for securing overlapping patterns, ranging from automatic boundary detection to free-hand painting and ghost-shape placement. **** #### **Glue Fill** Automatically detects the boundaries of a pattern or an internal shape to apply glue. Placing the secondary pattern in the 2D or 3D window defines the glue area between the patterns. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 2D Window** 1. Position the secondary pattern (the piece to be glued) directly **on top** of the base pattern. 2. Ensure the patterns overlap exactly where you want the bond to be established. 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100441)Glue Fill** tool and click on the secondary pattern or the secondary pattern’s internal shape(if any). → The overlap establishes the bonding relationship between the two layers. 4. Move the secondary outside the base pattern (optional). **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 3D Window** 1. If the patterns are not draped, position the secondary pattern over the base pattern. 2. If the garment is draped, then the secondary pattern must be **draped over or under** the base pattern (in contact or close proximity). 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100441)Glue Fill** tool and click on the secondary pattern. → The glue will be applied to the respective contact area between the layers. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **Set Options** 1. Set the mode if needed. **Add** | Applies glue to the whole pattern shape or its internal shape. ---|--- **Subtract** | Completely removes glue from the pattern. #### **Glue Brush** Allows for free-hand drawing of glue onto the pattern. The tool requires a layered relationship between two patterns to function. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 2D Window** 1. Position the secondary pattern (the piece to be glued) directly **on top** of the base pattern. 2. Ensure the patterns overlap in the area where you want the glue to be applied. 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100569)****Glue Brush** tool and click and drag on the pattern to paint the glue area, which appears as an orange highlight. 4. Once the desired area is painted, the secondary pattern will follow the movement and deformation of the painted area on the base fabric during simulation. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 3D Window** 1. If the patterns are not draped, position the secondary pattern over the base pattern. 2. If the garment is draped, then the secondary pattern must be **draped over or under** the base pattern (in contact or close proximity). 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100569)****Glue Brush** tool and click and drag on the pattern to paint the glue area, which appears as an orange highlight. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **Set Options** 1. Set the options if needed. **Type** | **Over** | Applies glue to the underside of the secondary pattern piece to bond with the pattern beneath it. ---|---|--- **Under** | Applies glue to the top surface of the base pattern piece to bond with the pattern above it. **Mode** | **Add** | Paint new adhesive areas onto the pattern surfaces. **Subtract** | Use this mode to partially remove existing glue by painting over the previously highlighted orange areas. **Size** | Allows you to adjust the width of the glue stroke for more precise or broader application. **** #### **Sticker** Mimics a real-world sticking process by allowing you to "pick up" a pattern piece and use a ghost pattern shape to precisely target and apply it to a specific area. 1. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55307548131481)****Sticker** tool in the 2D window. 2. Click on the desired secondary pattern piece (e.g., a pocket or label) to select it. 3. A **ghost pattern shape** (transparent preview) will appear and follow your cursor. 4. Move the ghost shape over the base pattern to target the desired placement area. 5. Click at the specific location on the base pattern to "stick" the piece in place. 6. View the results immediately in the 3D window as the pattern conforms to the target area. **** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569267938841) #### **Edit Gluing** #### Modify the position, scale, or rotation of the glued area of a pattern without disrupting the current adhesive connection. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 2D Window** 1. Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59493807792153)**Edit Glue** tool and click on the glued secondary pattern. → A bounding box appears with move, scale, and rotate handles. 2. Transform the pattern as needed. → The glue area updates in real time in both the 2D and 3D windows. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **2D Right-Click Options** Right-clicking a selected glued pattern in the 2D window shows the following options: **Option** | **Sub-option / Shortcut** | **Description** ---|---|--- **Delete** | Del | Removes the glue from the selected pattern. **Rotate** | Clockwise (45°) | Ctrl+Right Clockwise (90°) | Ctrl+Down Counterclockwise (45°) | Ctrl+Left Counterclockwise (90°) | Ctrl+Up **Flip** | Horizontally | Mirrors the glue area horizontally. Vertically | Mirrors the glue area vertically. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **3D Right-Click Options** Right-clicking on a primary glued pattern in the 3D window shows the following options: * **Superimpose Over** — Places the selected pattern on top of the glued pattern pair along its surface. * **Superimpose Under** — Places the selected pattern beneath the glued pattern pair. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **Property Editor** When a glued pattern is selected with the Edit Glue tool, the Property Editor displays the following: **Property** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Auto-assigned identifier for the glue object (e.g. Glue_001). Editable. **Strength** | Controls the bond strength of the glue area. Default: 1.000. **Thickness (mm)** | Sets the physical thickness offset of the glued layer. Default: 0.0.
content_description: Discover advanced bonding techniques with the new Glue Fill, Glue Brush, and Sticker tools in 2026.0, designed to seamlessly attach and manipulate pattern pieces during simulation for enhanced creativity and precision in garment design.

title: Pleats
content: **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RSYTLRsnzM ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats**** **2D Toolbar ▶**![Pleats.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360059605713/Pleats.png) Pleats** **** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- ** Specification ** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Create Notch | Select where to create Notch (Both, Start, or End). Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. (ver 6.0) **※ Note: **If the segment where pleats to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn. If the segment is not sewn, use the [Pleats Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307468-%ED%94%8C%EB%A6%AC%EC%B8%A0-%EC%A0%91%EA%B8%B0-%EC%9E%AC%EB%B4%89) tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on creating and customizing pleats in 2D patterns, including step-by-step instructions and options for different pleat types and configurations.

title: Transform Graphic (2D)

title: Polygon
content: ### **Objective** Create polygon Patterns in 2D Window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Polygon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165135793049) **Polygon** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Polygon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165135793049) **Polygon** 2. Click on the 2D window to make the start point. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand a polygon. 4. Right click while freehanding a polygon. → The Create Polygon window appears. 5. **Length** or **Mirror Creation** options to create polygon more precisely and conveniently. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Length** | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the **Mirror Creation** option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. **Option** **(ver5.0.0)** | Mirror Creation | The polygon is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. 6. Click again on the start point to complete the polygon. **※ Note:** * Pressing the keyboard’s Delete key while setting points to create a pattern cancels the points, starting from the most recent one. Furthermore, pressing the Esc/Ctrl+Z key during creation cancels the entire operation. * While making points to create a Pattern, holding down the Ctrl key and setting points turns segment points into Free Curve Points. This creates a polygon Pattern made up of curved lines. * Setting a Segment Point while holding down shift reveals a guideline that can move horizontally, vertically, and diagonally at a 45 degree angle according to the Segment Point.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to create custom polygon patterns in a 2D design window using the specified tools and options.

title: Fold Arrangement
content: ### **Objective** Fold Seam Allowances, collars and cuffs before activating the **Simulation** for better stability. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ **Fold** ▶ **Fold Arrangement** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Fold Arrangement.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53145879346713)**Fold Arrangement** **Operation** 1. After arranging Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ **Fold** ▶ **Fold Arrangement** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Fold Arrangement.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53145879346713)**Fold Arrangement** → The entire Internal Line/Shape of a 3D Garment appears. 2. Click on an Internal Line/Shape to fold. → The folding **Gizmo** appears. 3. Rotate the red or green axis along the blue circle as desired. → The selected pattern area is folded accordingly. → If the pattern is symmetrical, it is folded symmetrically. (ver 6.1) **※ Note:** Folding Internal Line/Shape is also available after simulating/draping the Garment.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions on how to properly fold seam allowances, collars, and cuffs in a 3D garment simulation for enhanced stability.

title: Copy/Paste Patterns (3D)
content: **Objective** Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window. ## ** **Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ **Copy** or **Paste** ## ** **Operation 1. Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024515248/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ **Copy** or **Paste** → A preview of the copied pattern follows the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the desired location in the 3D window to place the duplicated pattern. → The copied pattern is automatically assigned a number. **※ Note:** * To copy and paste more efficiently, select the pattern, press Ctrl+C, then press Ctrl+V or Ctrl+R on the keyboard to copy, paste or mirror paste, respectively. * Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window to another CLO software window (ver3.0.0). This is only available in Windows. * Trims and buttons are also copied and pasted along with Patterns (ver5.0.0.) * In the case of buttons and/or subsidiary materials in the pattern, they cannot be copied and pasted into other programs.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for efficiently copying and pasting patterns within the 3D window of CLO software, enabling users to enhance their design workflow.

title: Isolate Selection
content: **New in 2026.0** **** Display only selected elements in the 3D window. 1. Select the desired elements and click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55430497110809)**Isolate Selection** or press **Shift + I**. → Only the selected remain visible in the 3D window. 2. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55430497112345) **Isolate Selection** or press **Shift + I** again to exit isolation mode. → The 3D window returns to the previous display state. #### **📝Note:** * Isolation uses the selection state at the moment it is activated and does not update automatically. * If Isolate Selection is applied with no elements selected, the 3D window appears empty. * To isolate a different selection. exit isolation mode, make a new selection, and activate Isolate Selection again. * Isolate Selection affects only the 3D window display and does not modify object Show/Hide properties or image render output.
content_description: Explore the new **Isolate Selection** feature in 2026.0 that allows you to focus on specific elements in the 3D window for a clearer design experience.

title: Open MetaHuman Body Types
content: ### **Objective** Select a desired MetaHuman body type and create an outfit for your MetaHuman in CLO before bringing the outfit to Unreal Engine as USD files. ### **Location** Library ▶ Click Avatar Folder ▶ MetaHuman ▶ Double click to download a desired MetaHuman body types ## **※ Note :** * Arms need to be bent on export in order for Unreal Engine's USD import pipeline to work properly. Once garments are ready to be exported, apply a pose named 'Default_Pose' in Pose folder to a desired MetaHuman body. * A pose named 'Apose' is provided in order for garments to be fit on a desired MetaHuman body with ease, especially around arms. * In Marvelous Designer versions below 2024.0.173, applying the two aforementioned poses to a MetaHuman body will result in the error message "No matching avatar" and will not be applied.
content_description: This web page guides users in selecting a MetaHuman body type and creating a compatible outfit in CLO for seamless export to Unreal Engine as USD files.

title: Mirror Paste
content: **Objective** Mirror Paste copied Pattern/Internal Shape. ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) ▶ **Mirror Paste**(Ctrl + R) ** Operation** 1. Navigate to 2D toolbar and select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005610407/_______.png) **Transform Pattern** Tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005661808/_______.png) **Edit Pattern** Tool. Then, copy the desired Pattern or Internal Shape. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) ▶ **Mirror Paste** (Ctrl + R) → The clone of copied Pattern/Internal Shape follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the 2D window or on the Pattern to place the Pattern or the Internal Shape. **※ Note: ** * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to move the duplicated Pattern on a straight line or on a diagonal line. * Select the desired Pattern and hit Ctrl + C (Copy) / Ctrl +V(Paste), Ctrl + R(Mirror Paste) on the keyboard to copy and paste Patterns to a separate CLO window (ver3.0.0).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to use the Mirror Paste function to duplicate and manipulate patterns or internal shapes in a 2D design environment.

title: Trace
content: **List of Contents** Trace Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes Trace as an Internal Shape Trace as an Internal Shape vs. Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes Trace as a Pattern Trace with Guidelines **Trace** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x9H8bsVBdVw \- Trace Baselines, Internal Lines and Pattern outlines as Internal Lines and Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022745867/mceclip0.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ **Trace.** ** Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** * **Select Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern Outlines YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-V27Rbjo5Yw **\- Click on the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines to be traced. \- Or, click and drag to encompass the desired items into the marquee box. \- The selected items will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rlYl0l0fn2k ** \- Right-click on the selected item and choose **Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** or**Trace as an Internal Shape.** **Trace as an Internal Shape** * **Select Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern Outlines YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=58R-Uhtuka4 ** \- To trace Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines as a shape, all selected lines need to be joined. \- Click on the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines to be traced. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select multiple items. \- Or, click and drag to encompass the desired items into the marquee box. \- The selected items will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3BoMdZaXDXQ ** \- Right-click on the selected item and choose Trace as **Internal Lines/ Shapes** or **Trace as an Internal Shape.** **Trace as an Internal Shape vs. Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** * **Trace as an Internal Shape YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=giYuoBwZzgk ** \- Use this option extract a closed shape as the shape created by the intersecting lines. \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines that form the desired shape. Then, right-click and select **Trace as an Internal Shape**. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746067/mceclip1.png)**Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and select the shape just traced. \- The closed shape will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TANzamZaeXY ** \- Use this option to trace intersecting lines as individual and separated lines. \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines to be traced. Then, right-click and select **Trace as an Internal Lines/ Shapes.** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746067/mceclip1.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and select the lines just traced. \- Each traced lines will be selected individually. **Trace as a Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y8252WGNMRQ \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines that form a shape. \- Right-click on the selected items and choose **Trace as Pattern.** \- To trace a shape as a Pattern, all lines’ ends need to be adjoining each other. \- When more than three intersecting lines are selected, a shape formed by them will be traced as a Pattern. **Trace with Guidelines_ver.5.0.0 and Above** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNLxAuFTYUM \- Select guidelines with Internal Lines or Pattern Outlines, and then right click to select the desired Trace option. \- Make sure to right click on the Internal Line or the Pattern Outline when tracing with guidelines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to using the Trace tool in 2D pattern design, detailing various tracing methods and providing instructional YouTube videos for each technique.

title: VRM Import/Export
content: ## **New in 2026.0** **** VRM file type is the most widely used 'universal format for 3D avatars' in the virtual metaverse. This is convenient 3D character file that allow you to import animation-style custom characters directly into the software without complex settings or conversion processes, enabling you to dress and fit garments while maintaining the character's unique appearance and movements. **📝 No****te:** The VRM file format is based on glTF 2.0, and the properties that can be controlled in the Import/Export VRM dialog box are identical to those of [**glTF 2.0**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360051525034-glTF-2-0-GLTF-GLB-File). #### **Import VRM** 1. Click **Main Menu** ▶ **File** ▶ **Import** ▶ **VRM** , specify the file path and name to display the Import VRM dialog. 2. Set the desired properties in the Import VRM dialog box, then click **OK** to load the file. #### #### **Export VRM** 1. Click **Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ VRM** , specify the destination path and file name to display the Export VRM dialog. 2. Set the properties in the Export VRM dialog box, then click **OK** to export the file. **📝****Note:** A VRM file can only be exported if it meets the following two conditions: * The top-level parent of the export target's joint root must form a single hierarchy. * It must have a humanoid skeleton structure.
content_description: Discover the convenience of the VRM file format for 3D avatars, enabling seamless import and export of animated characters in the virtual metaverse without the hassle of complex settings.

title: How to Fix the Error using Intel Graphics Card
content: **List of Contents** Case 1 Case 2 (If the error is not resolved by Case 1) Objective Learn how to resolve launching error using Intel HD Graphics. Operation Since this crashing is due to a Graphic driver which is automatically updated by Microsoft Windows, please re-install the Intel graphics driver after deactivating "Windows Automatic Updates". Case 1 1. Please input "gpedit.msc" on Search tool and execute it. 2. Local Group Policy Editor ▶ Computer Configuration ▶ Administrative Templates ▶ Windows Components ▶ Windows Updates ▶ activate "Do not include drivers with Windows Update" ![image_1_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003369948/image_1_1.png)**※ Note:** The option may not appear in the Window versions below. In this case, External Graphics card should be used. (Please refer to [Computer Specification](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-Computer-Specifications)) Windows 7 Home Edition / Windows 10 Home Edition 3. Device Manager ▶ Display Adapters ▶ Intel(R) HD Graphic ▶ Uninstall the device and driver software ▶ Reboot Windows ![image_2_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003447047/image_2_1.png) 4. Enter [Intel Support Page](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/intel-driver-support-assistant.html) and download and install the program of Intel® Driver & Support Assistant. 5. Start scanning the driver. 6. Download and Reinstall the driver of Intel(R) HD Graphics. 7. Verify the "23.20.16.4901" version is installed correctly.![image_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003369968/image_3.png) 8. Please reboot Windows. 9. If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2 below. **Case 2** If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2. 1. Please enter [Intel® Graphics Driver for Windows*](https://downloadcenter.intel.com/download/27412/Graphics-Intel-Graphics-Driver-for-Windows-15-60-?wapkw=hd+graphic) and Download & Install the driver. 2. Approve overwrite to the previous version during Installation. ![image_3_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003369988/image_3_1.png) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for resolving launching errors caused by Intel HD Graphics drivers, including troubleshooting methods for both initial and unresolved issues.

title: Edit Measurement
content: ### **Objective** Edit avatar measurements. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Measure Tab** ### **Operation ** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Measure Tab**** ** → The list of avatar measurements created on the active Avatar appears. 2. Click on the measurement to see or edit its properties. **Name** | Rename the measurement. | **Basic Length** | Check the measurement's basic length. ---|---|---|--- **Measurement Type** | Change the measurement type. | **Surface Length** | Check the surface length of the measurement. **Measurement Information** | Check the measurement's information. | **Show** | Show or hide the selected measurement.

title: Edit Line (3D Pattern)
content: **List of Contents** Edit Line (3D Pattern) Edit 3D Line Delete 3D Line Right Click Pop-Up Menu on 3D Line **Edit Line (3D Pattern)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpjX25UuBao \- Select, delete and Edit 3D lines created on draped Garments in the 3D Window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021985308/mceclip0.png) **Edit line (3D Line)** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Edit 3D Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JaqfRrmvwxI \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021985308/mceclip0.png) **Edit Line (3D Line)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click and drag the point on the 3D Line to make adjustments. **Delete 3D Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K5DyjtZDnxA \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021985308/mceclip0.png) **Edit Line (3D Line)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click on the 3D Line, then hit the Delete key or the Backspace key on the keyboard to delete. **Right Click Pop-up Menu on 3D Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iVlsF--JXgY \- Right-click on the 3D Line to access the pop-up menu and select options as below for desired actions. * **Delete** \- The selected 3D Line will be deleted. * **Cut** \- Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- When a 3D Line is drawn only on one of the symmetric Patterns, only the Pattern with the 3D Line will be cut and the linked editing function will be removed. * **Cut & Sew** \- Cut and Sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- When a 3D Line is drawn only on one of the symmetric Patterns, only the Pattern with the 3D Line will be cut and sewn and the linked editing function will be removed. * **(Symmetry) Cut** \- Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- Even if the selected 3D Line is drawn on only one of the Symmetric Patterns, both Symmetric Patterns will be cut and linked editing function will be maintained. * **(Symmetry) Cut & Sew** \- Cut and Sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- Even if the selected 3D Line is drawn on only one of the Symmetric Patterns, both Symmetric Patterns will be cut and sewn and linked editing function will be maintained. * **Trace as Internal Shape** \- Trace the selected 3D Line as an Internal Shape. * **Convert to Internal Shape** \- Convert the selected 3D Lines to an Internal Shape. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive guidance on editing, deleting, and managing 3D lines in garment design, complete with instructional YouTube videos for each function.
